content: SANDBOX → stack.templetwo.com 502s — ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE confirmed 2026-05-28 by Claude 4.7 web seat. Bimodal Cloudflare edge routing at the ORD colo. (1) From the Anthropic sandbox, ~45% of requests to stack.templetwo.com return Cloudflare 502 — across BOTH /api/heartbeat GET (30% failure) and /api/call POST (35% h2 / 60% h1.1 failure). (2) N=40 sample clustered by cf-ray suffix shows PERFECT bimodal split: all 200s on suffix 1477-ORD, all 502s on suffix 99f0-ORD, zero crossover. Two distinct Cloudflare edge shards in Chicago are serving the same hostname; one healthy, one broken. (3) 502 evidence proves Cloudflare-generated not origin-generated: 15-byte stock "error code: 502\\n" body in text/plain (not the JSON shape FastAPI returns), 150-250ms latency identical to 200s (origin timeout would be 10s+), no cf-ray or origin marker in body. The failing shard never proxies to origin. (4) HQ does not see this because anycast routes Plymouth Meeting traffic to EWR/LGA, not ORD; the broken shard is invisible from the operator seat. (5) Workaround: retry on 5xx — same-connection keepalive sticks to one shard, closing/reopening rerolls. Expected calls to first success ~1.8. (6) Real fix belongs on Anthony side: open Cloudflare dashboard for stack.templetwo.com, filter to last 24h colo=ORD, look for 5xx spike on the broken edge; check Worker deploy log for partial propagation; check Cloudflare Tunnel health. (7) The Anthropic sandbox-egress TLS inspector (O=Anthropic, CN=sandbox-egress-production TLS Inspection CA, cert issued May 28 23:56:45 2026 GMT, expires Jun 27 23:56:44 2026 GMT) is REAL and applies to all sandbox outbound — but it is NOT the cause of these 502s. It applies identically to healthy and failing shards.
